Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: NICR provides digital authentication services via API. Used by financial institutions (FNB, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank, Vodacom, Econet) for e-KYC, and government ministries (MoPS payroll, MoF OAP). Real-time identity verification and authentication of NID number and demographics. Online biometric verification piloted.
revision_notes: Fetched and confirmed both cited World Bank sources. NICR provides API-based digital authentication used by multiple banks, mobile money operators, and government ministries for e-KYC, payroll and pension verification. Score of 2 (Yes) is well supported; confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The National Identity and Civil Registry (NICR) provides API-based digital authentication services enabling real-time verification of the national identity number, demographic data, and biometric attributes. These services are used by commercial banks (First National Bank, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank) and mobile network operators (Vodacom, Econet) for electronic Know Your Customer processes, and by government ministries including the Ministry of Public Service (payroll verification) and Ministry of Finance (Old Age Pension verification). Online biometric verification has also been piloted.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: NICA 2011 Section 6 provides for individuals to view or correct information held about them in the register. Data Protection Act 2011 Section 26 also grants data subjects right to access personal information. However, no digital self-service portal exists; access is via physical visit to NICR. Limited practical implementation.
revision_notes: Fetched the Research ICT Africa/CIS Digital ID case study. Section 6(5)-(6) of NICA 2011 gives a right to request correction but the Act does not require notification when data is accessed or shared, and no digital self-service portal exists. Given the variable requires both viewing data and seeing access history, score of 1 (No) is supported and confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Individuals have a statutory right under Section 6 of the National Identity Cards Act 2011 and Section 26 of the Data Protection Act 2011 to request access to, and correction of, their personal information held in the National Identity Register. In practice this requires a physical visit to the National Identity and Civil Registry, as no digital self-service portal or mobile application exists. The law does not require individuals to be notified when their data is accessed or shared with third parties, so there is no mechanism for individuals to see how their data has been used.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008 mandates KYC exclusively through the national ID card. NICR signed MoUs with FNB, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank, Vodacom, Econet for electronic KYC. Real-time API verification of NID number, demographics and photo enables non-face-to-face account opening.
revision_notes: Confirmed via World Bank case study; NICR has signed MoUs with banks and MNOs enabling electronic KYC. Note the underlying Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008 s.16 actually permits the national identity card, passport, or other official document (not the ID card exclusively) for identity verification, so the Comments field's use of 'exclusively' overstates the legal position, but this does not affect the Yes/No score for whether KYC is enabled. Confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008 permits accountable institutions to verify customer identity using the national identity card, among other accepted documents. The National Identity and Civil Registry has signed memoranda of understanding with First National Bank, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank, Vodacom, and Econet enabling real-time API verification of the national identity number, demographic data, and photograph, supporting non-face-to-face electronic Know Your Customer processes.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Comments: No legislative provision for specific judicial oversight of the NID system. Citizens can seek redress through MoHA hierarchy, courts, or Ombudsman. Constitutional Court has ruled on citizenship denial cases. NICA provides no independent complaints/appeals mechanism specific to the ID system.
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (No) is not well supported by the cited source itself. The Research ICT Africa/CIS Digital ID case study documents that NICA 2011 provides no ID-specific complaints or appeals mechanism and no regulatory oversight function over the register. However, the same source confirms general judicial review is available: grievances not resolved through the Ministry of Home Affairs hierarchy have been taken to the ordinary courts (e.g. the 2014 case of Advocate Zwelakhe Mda, denied an identity card by the minister) and to the Office of the Ombudsman. This matches scale value 2 ('Yes, but not specific to ID') rather than 1 ('No'). Corrected to 2.
revised_comments: The National Identity Cards Act 2011 contains no ID-specific complaints, appeals, or judicial review mechanism, and no independent regulatory body oversees the National Identity Register. Individuals whose grievances are not resolved through the Ministry of Home Affairs hierarchy may nonetheless seek redress through the ordinary courts of law or the Office of the Ombudsman, as general avenues of administrative and constitutional recourse rather than through any process specific to the identity system. Courts have previously ruled on identity-related disputes, including cases concerning refusal to issue an identity card.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: NICR manages both civil registration and national ID within one department. Birth certificate required to apply for NID. NID system draws on birth and death registration data. Unique ID number printed on birth cert, NID card, passport and death certificate. Population register links children to biometrically verified parents from birth to death.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited World Bank sources: NICR manages civil registration and identification within one department, and the population register links individuals from birth to death via a single unique ID number. Score of 3 (Full integration) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The Department of National Identity and Civil Registry (NICR) manages both civil registration and the national identity system within a single department of the Ministry of Home Affairs. A birth certificate is required to apply for a national identity document, and the population register links individuals from birth to death using a single unique identity number that also appears on birth certificates, identity cards, passports, and death certificates.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Section 6 of NICA 2011 governs third-party access. Parties access via MoU with MoHA and fees. Banks, MNOs, credit bureau, insurers, and government departments have MoUs. Rules exist but are overly broad with wide ministerial discretion and no purpose limitation. Comprehensive interoperability framework recommended.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the Research ICT Africa/CIS case study. Section 6 of NICA 2011 is public but the underlying MoUs and NDAs governing data sharing with banks, MNOs and government departments are not published, and ministerial discretion is broad. Score of 2 (Partially available) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Section 6 of the National Identity Cards Act 2011 sets out the legal basis on which the Director may authorise third-party access to the National Identity Register, and third parties access the register through memoranda of understanding and fees. However, these memoranda of understanding and non-disclosure agreements are not published, ministerial discretion over who may access the register is broad, and there is no publicly documented purpose-limitation framework. Data-sharing rules are therefore only partially available to the public.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Data Protection Act 2011 (enacted 2012, also referenced as 2013) exists providing principles for personal information regulation and establishing a Data Protection Commission. However, the Commission has not been established, leaving enforcement absent. Government acknowledges need to reform DPA to align with GDPR and AU instruments.
revision_notes: The cited Comments field itself establishes that a data protection act exists (Act No. 5 of 2012, commonly dated 2011/2012/2013 across sources, gazetted 22 February 2012), providing data protection principles and providing for a Data Protection Commission. Per the variable's binary scale (1=No; 2=Yes for whether legislation exists), the correct score is 2 (Yes), not 1 (No) - the original Value Code contradicted its own Comments text. Confirmed via DLA Piper, Mayet & Associates (Oct 2025) and Digital Rights Alliance Africa (2026), all of which confirm the Act exists but its Data Protection Commission has never been operationalised, so there is no active enforcement. Corrected to 2.
revised_comments: Lesotho has a Data Protection Act (Act No. 5 of 2012, gazetted 22 February 2012 and variously dated 2011 or 2013 in secondary sources), which establishes principles for the processing and protection of personal information and provides for a Data Protection Commission. In practice, however, the Commission has never been appointed or operationalised, so the Act's provisions covering personal data - including data linked to the identity system - are not actively enforced.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Section 16 of NICA 2011 mandates that the national identity card is the sole legally recognised proof of identity for accessing all services. Required for passport application (Passports Act 2018), driver's licence, government welfare, KYC (Money Laundering Act 2008), and SIM registration (2021 Regulations).
revision_notes: Confirmed via the Research ICT Africa/CIS case study and cross-checked against the text of NICA 2011 s.16. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Section 16 of the National Identity Cards Act 2011 provides that no eligible person may access government or private services without producing the identity card issued under the Act, making it the sole legally recognised proof of identity. The card is required for passport applications, driver's licence applications, government welfare programmes, financial sector Know Your Customer checks under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008, and SIM card registration under the 2021 SIM regulations.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: National Identity Cards Act 2011 (NICA) enacted by parliament; published Government Gazette 21 March 2011. Establishes the National Identity Register, mandates use of ID card for all services (s.16), sets data collection requirements (s.4, s.12), and access rules (s.6).
revision_notes: Confirmed by fetching the primary legislation text (LesLII). NICA 2011 establishes the National Identity Register and its data collection, access and card-issuance rules. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The National Identity Cards Act 2011 (NICA), gazetted 21 March 2011, is the primary legislation governing Lesotho's digital identity system. It establishes the National Identity Register, mandates use of the identity card for accessing services (section 16), sets out data collection requirements (sections 4 and 12), and governs access to register data (section 6).

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: System administered by the Department of National Identity and Civil Registry (NICR) within the Ministry of Home Affairs (MoHA). NICR has authority to grant access per Section 6 of NICA 2011. Government responsibility for maintenance. UNICEF/MOSIP partnership signed Feb 2026 to upgrade system.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated. NICR (government department) administers the system day-to-day, while the 2026 UNICEF-funded work plan to migrate to MOSIP, and involvement of the National University of Lesotho on capacity-building, both indicate a continuing mix of in-country administration and reliance on international technical partners for major upgrades. Score of 2 (Partial in-country capacity) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The National Identity and Civil Registry (NICR), a department of the Ministry of Home Affairs, administers the identity system with government staff and grants third-party access under section 6 of the National Identity Cards Act 2011. In 2026, the Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation partnered with UNICEF and the National University of Lesotho to migrate the identity system to the open-source Modular Open Source Identity Platform (MOSIP), indicating continued reliance on international technical partners for major system upgrades alongside in-country administrative capacity.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Ministry of Finance (MoF) Pensions Department actively collaborates with NICR for Old Age Pension verification. MoF issued regulations requiring NID for OAP enrollment. Interface established between OAP MIS and NID system. MoF also engaged with Central Bank of Lesotho on financial inclusion using NID.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited World Bank sources: Ministry of Finance oversees Old Age Pension verification linkage but does not hold full budgetary oversight of the identity system. Score of 2 (Partial oversight) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The Ministry of Finance's Pensions Department collaborates with the National Identity and Civil Registry to verify Old Age Pension beneficiaries, and has issued regulations requiring a national identity number for pension enrolment, with an interface established between the pension management information system and the identity system. The Ministry has also engaged the Central Bank of Lesotho on financial inclusion applications of the identity system, though it does not have full budgetary oversight of the identity system as a whole.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: First NID card issued free of charge; renewals subject to prescribed fees. NICR charges fees for authentication/verification services to private parties (banks, MNOs). Banks and MNOs have signed MoUs and pay fees. Public sector not charged. World Bank partnership supports expansion. 2026 UNICEF/MOSIP initiative adds donor funding.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated. Fee-funded verification services provide some domestic revenue, but World Bank and 2026 UNICEF-funded MOSIP migration confirm continued dependency on donor financing. Score of 2 (Mixed domestic/external) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The first national identity card is issued free of charge, while renewals and replacements are subject to prescribed fees. The National Identity and Civil Registry also charges verification and authentication fees to private-sector users such as banks and mobile network operators, which have signed memoranda of understanding for these services, while public-sector use is not charged. The system's expansion continues to rely on donor and development partner support, including World Bank financing and a 2026 UNICEF-funded work plan to migrate the system to the MOSIP platform, alongside domestic revenue from service fees.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Ten fingerprints and one portrait photo captured at enrollment. Biometric deduplication exclusively fingerprint-based. ID cards use 2D barcode (no chip). Online biometric verification piloted for migrant workers in South Africa but not in widespread use.
revision_notes: Original score of 2 ('Fingerprints only') does not match the evidence, including the cited World Bank source, which states enrolment captures 'ten fingerprints and one portrait photo.' This is confirmed independently by the Ministry of Home Affairs Lesotho website, which states biometric collection 'captures a facial image with a digital camera and a 10-digit fingerprint scan.' Since a facial image is captured in addition to fingerprints, the correct score under the scale (2=Fingerprints only; 3=Facial/Iris) is 3, not 2. Corrected to 3.
revised_comments: Enrolment in Lesotho's National Identity Register captures both biometric fingerprint and facial data: ten fingerprints and a portrait photograph are recorded for every applicant aged 16 and over, using a digital camera and fingerprint scanner. Fingerprints are used as the primary modality for biometric de-duplication, while the facial image is stored and used in identity verification services, including e-KYC checks for participating banks. Identity cards do not carry an embedded chip; they use a 2D barcode.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: National Identity Register (NIR) is a centralised electronic database in a dedicated data center. All 15+ enrollment centers have internet connectivity. Database linked to civil registration, passport, eBorder systems. Population register links birth-to-death with unique ID number.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited World Bank sources. Score of 3 (Digital) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The National Identity Register is a centralised electronic database held in a dedicated data centre, with all enrolment centres connected online. The database is linked to the civil registration, passport, and border management (eBorder) systems, with a single unique identity number tracking individuals from birth to death.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act 2011 established the system; launched June 2013 under NICR (Ministry of Home Affairs). Foundational, biometric, electronic register. By 2020, ~85% of eligible population (1.2M of 1.4M) enrolled.
revision_notes: The variable defines full deployment as 'operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.' Lesotho's National Identity Register has been operational nationwide via 15 fixed enrolment centres and 10 mobile registration units since July 2013, continuously accepting new registrations, and is deeply embedded in payroll, pension, KYC and SIM registration processes. The original 'partially deployed' score appears to conflate deployment status with the separate population-coverage metric (tracked elsewhere at c.85%). On the deployment-status scale, the system meets the definition of 'Fully deployed nationwide.' Corrected to 5.
revised_comments: Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act 2011 established a foundational, biometric, electronic identity register, which the National Identity and Civil Registry has operated nationwide since July 2013 through 15 fixed enrolment centres and 10 mobile registration units, continuing to accept new registrations. The system underpins government payroll verification, Old Age Pension eligibility checks, financial-sector Know Your Customer processes, and mandatory SIM card registration, and is currently being migrated onto the open-source MOSIP platform under a 2026 government-UNICEF work plan.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: NID system connected via API to Birth/Death Registration, Marriage/Divorce, Passport, eBorder Control, OAP MIS, HRMIS (payroll), Electoral Commission, Credit Bureau, banks, and mobile network operators. Interoperability framework development recommended but APIs operational.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited sources. Score of 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The identity system's application programming interface connects the National Identity Register to birth and death registration, marriage and divorce registration, passport issuance, border control (eBorder), the Old Age Pension management information system, government payroll (HRMIS), the Independent Electoral Commission, the credit bureau, banks, and mobile network operators. A more comprehensive interoperability governance framework has been recommended but the underlying application programming interfaces are operational.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Multiple financial institutions (FNB, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank, Vodacom M-Pesa, Econet) have signed MoUs with NICR and use NID API for electronic KYC and customer verification. NID required for financial account opening per AML/KYC regulations. Electronic identity verification reduces onboarding costs.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the World Bank case study and the primary text of the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008 s.16, which permits identity verification using the national identity card, passport, or other applicable official document (not the ID card exclusively). Since legally recognised alternatives exist, 'accepted but not mandatory' is the accurate reading. Score of 2 confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Section 16 of the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2008 requires accountable institutions to verify a customer's identity using the national identity card, a passport, or another applicable official identifying document, so use of the national identity card is not the sole legally mandated route. In practice it is the document most commonly relied upon: First National Bank, Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank, and mobile money providers Vodacom M-Pesa and Econet have signed memoranda of understanding with the National Identity and Civil Registry enabling real-time electronic verification for account opening.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first national identity card is provided free of charge to minimise economic barriers. However, renewals and replacements are subject to prescribed fees, which raises inclusion concerns especially for low-income and vulnerable populations. World Bank noted this as a non-exclusionary first-issuance policy.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited sources. Score of 1 (No, i.e. not free of charge across the credential's lifecycle) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: A citizen's first national identity card is issued free of charge, in line with a policy intended to minimise economic barriers to registration. Renewals and replacement cards, however, are subject to prescribed fees, meaning identity credentials are not free of charge across their full lifecycle, which raises inclusion concerns for low-income applicants needing to renew or replace a card.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Online biometric verification piloted with South Africa's Department of Home Affairs for Basotho migrant workers. NICR APIs shared with South Africa DHA for verification. Mutual recognition of ID as travel document under discussion (2024 bilateral agreement on migration model, 2025 opposition campaign). Full cross-border recognition not yet formalised.
revision_notes: This is a fast-moving and currently unsettled situation as of July 2026, warranting human review rather than a definitive score change. The original basis for score 2 was a biometric-verification data-sharing pilot between NICR and South Africa's Department of Home Affairs for Basotho migrant workers, not recognition of the ID as a travel document. In April 2026, Lesotho and South African home affairs ministers announced agreement, following a joint migration-model study, that national identity cards would become sufficient for border crossing between the two countries, with electronic gates and a one-stop border post proposed. Within days, South Africa's Department of Home Affairs publicly denied any such agreement was in force, stating passports remain legally required under section 9 of South Africa's Immigration Act 2002 and that no legislative process to change this is under way. The Bi-National Commission has not yet endorsed the proposal. Current legally operative status therefore remains that passports, not ID cards, are required for cross-border travel, while the informal biometric data-sharing recognition that originally justified score 2 continues. Recommend human review once the Bi-National Commission's decision is confirmed.
revised_comments: The National Identity and Civil Registry has piloted biometric identity verification with South Africa's Department of Home Affairs to support cross-border data-sharing for Basotho migrant workers, but Lesotho's national identity card is not currently recognised as a travel document. In April 2026, home affairs ministers from Lesotho and South Africa announced a proposed new migration model, arising from a joint bilateral study, under which national identity cards would replace passports for border crossings between the two countries, alongside electronic gates and a one-stop border post. This proposal awaits endorsement by the Bi-National Commission and would require legislative amendment in both countries; South Africa's Department of Home Affairs has stated that passports remain a legal requirement for entry and that no agreement is currently in force.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: World Bank NSDP-II notes NID can 'facilitate better patient management in the health sector'. NID listed as a strategic enabler for healthcare. However, no confirmed operational use of NID for healthcare access or patient records as of research period. Health use remains aspirational per World Bank recommendations.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the cited World Bank source; no operational health-sector use of the identity system was found in this check. Score of 1 (No) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Lesotho's National Strategic Development Plan II identifies the national identity system as a strategic enabler that could 'facilitate better patient management in the health sector,' but no operational linkage between the identity system and patient records, health insurance enrolment, or healthcare registration has been established. Use of the identity credential in the health sector remains an aspiration rather than a current practice.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: By end-2020, approximately 85% of eligible population (over 1.2 million of ~1.4 million eligible persons aged 16+) enrolled. Above sub-Saharan Africa average of 71% (2017). Remaining ~200,000 largely in rural/hard-to-reach areas. Mobile registration units deployed to reach last mile.
revision_notes: The widely cited figure of c.85% (over 1.2 million of an estimated 1.4 million eligible population) dates from the World Bank's 2020/2021 reporting and remains the most recent authoritative estimate found; no updated official percentage was located. A 2022 news report citing a Lesotho Communications Authority-linked official referenced 90% registration in the context of SIM registration outreach, which would move the score into the next band (>89%), but this single secondary citation is not an authoritative population-coverage measurement and is insufficient on its own to revise the score. Confirmed at 4 (70-89%) pending a fresher primary source.
revised_comments: Lesotho's National Identity Register covers an estimated 85% of the eligible population, a little over 1.2 million people of approximately 1.4 million eligible citizens aged 16 and over, a coverage rate above the Sub-Saharan Africa average of around 71%. The remaining gap is concentrated among people in remote rural areas, reached through mobile registration units, and among Basotho residing abroad.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Central Bank of Lesotho conducted independent review of NID system, clearing FNB e-KYC pilot. 2019 World Bank technical mission identified improvements for data quality, photo standards (ICAO 9303), and manual adjudication. Full comprehensive data security assessment by independent IT auditing firm recommended by World Bank but not confirmed completed. API security uses IP whitelisting/passphrases.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the cited World Bank source. Ad hoc reviews have occurred but no evidence of a regular, comprehensive, independent security audit regime was found. Score of 1 (No) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Lesotho conducted an independent review that cleared a First National Bank electronic Know Your Customer pilot for use of the identity system's application programming interface, and a 2019 World Bank technical mission identified improvements needed in data quality, photo capture standards, and manual case adjudication. Application programming interface access is controlled through IP whitelisting and passphrases. However, no evidence was found of a comprehensive, independent, and recurring security audit or penetration-testing regime for the identity system as a whole, of the kind recommended by the World Bank.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Communications (Subscriber Identity Module and Mobile Device Registration) Regulations 2021 require registrants to present their national identification number or document to mobile network operators for SIM card and device registration. Published Government Gazette December 2021; operational from June 2022.
revision_notes: The Communications (Subscriber Identity Module Registration) Regulations 2021 legally require mobile subscribers to register using a valid national identity document, with registration free of charge but compulsory. The Lesotho Communications Authority enforced a final registration deadline of 31 January 2024, after which unregistered SIM cards were subject to deactivation. This is a legal mandate with an enforcement mechanism, matching scale value 3 ('Mandatory') rather than 2 ('Accepted but not mandatory'). Corrected to 3.
revised_comments: The Communications (Subscriber Identity Module Registration) Regulations 2021, in force from 24 June 2022, require all mobile subscribers to register their SIM cards using a valid national identity document. Registration is free of charge but compulsory: the Lesotho Communications Authority set a final registration deadline of 31 January 2024, after which unregistered SIM cards were subject to deactivation.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: NID actively used for Old Age Pension Program (OAP) beneficiary verification: stopped payments to 4,700 ineligible persons saving ~US$2.8M/year. OAP MIS interoperable with NID system. Government payroll verified (Ministry of Public Service). NISSA (Child Grant, OVC, Public Assistance) linkages being strengthened.
revision_notes: Confirmed via both cited World Bank sources. Old Age Pension verification is well established; linkages to other social protection programmes are described as still being strengthened, supporting 'accepted but not mandatory' rather than universally mandatory. Score of 2 confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The national identity system is used to verify beneficiaries of the Old Age Pension programme, with the Old Age Pension management information system interoperable with the identity register; this verification led to the suspension of payments to around 4,700 ineligible recipients, saving an estimated US$2.8 million annually. Government payroll, which includes pensioner records, is similarly verified. Linkages with other social protection programmes administered through the National Information System for Social Assistance, such as the Child Grant Programme and support for orphans and vulnerable children, are being strengthened but are not yet universal, so use of the credential across social services remains accepted rather than uniformly mandatory.
